system_note: What was billed: Principal Dx billed as K85.90 (acute pancreatitis, unspecified) with additional pancreatitis codes K85.11 (biliary acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) and K85.82 (acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis), sepsis/septic shock codes (R65.21, A41.50, B96.1), respiratory failure/ARDS codes (J96.01, J80), and procedures including endotracheal intubation and >96-hour ventilation (0BH17EZ; 5A1D90Z). What the record actually documents (key citations): - Infected pancreatic necrosis with identified organism (Klebsiella pneumoniae) and biliary/gallstone etiology: History & Physical (Admitting) active problem list contains "2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae" and "Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology." (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946). These items establish infected, gallstone-related necrotizing pancreatitis rather than an uninfected necrosis or non-specific pancreatitis. (See evidence excerpts below.) - Microbiology/treatment and source control consistent with infected necrosis: Discharge/Transfer Summary documents "infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16," confirming an organism-identified infection that was managed (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086). - Septic shock physiology on admission and vasopressor support: Admission labs and orders show elevated lactate ("lactate 4.6 mmol/L") and nursing/provider orders include vasopressor support ("norepinephrine to MAP >= 65") (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946). The Hospital Problem List lists "Septic shock | R65.21 | 05/29/2026 | Resolved | Off vasopressors day 10," indicating septic shock onset on admission (Hospital Problem List, Hospital Problem List, p. 9-9). - Respiratory failure and mechanical ventilation: multiple ICU progress notes and a Procedure Note document intubation for respiratory failure (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p. 44-44: "Indication for Procedure: Respiratory failure from pancreatitis and pain") and the Discharge Summary documents extubation on ICU day 18 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086), establishing ventilatory support >96 hours and supporting J96.01 and the ventilator-duration procedure code. Why this fails as billed (policy + documentation linkage): 1) Conflicting pancreatitis codes / principal diagnosis specificity: the chart documents necrotizing, infected, gallstone pancreatitis with organism identified. Coding both K85.11 (biliary acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) and K85.82 (acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis) on the same stay is internally inconsistent (one states uninfected necrosis, the other infected necrosis). Further, the principal diagnosis billed as K85.90 (unspecified) is less specific than the record supports. The record supports a specific infected necrotizing biliary pancreatitis as the principal diagnosis (see Admission H&P and Discharge Summary) - therefore principal should be the infected necrosis code (K85.82) rather than K85.90 or the uninfected code K85.11 (contradicted by the clinical documentation cited). 2) Sepsis organism specificity and sepsis/septic-shock coding: the microbiology and provider documentation identify Klebsiella pneumoniae as the infecting organism and the team treated with meropenem (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086; History & Physical active problem list). The R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) documentation requirements in policy require provider documentation of septic shock plus objective evidence (vasopressor use, lactate elevation) - all present in the chart (Policy: Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx; see criterion for vasopressor + lactate). Given the organism is identified, the appropriate organism-specific A41 code is A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) rather than A41.50 (gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) combined with B96.1. The policy ICD-10 selection guide explicitly lists Klebsiella pneumoniae -> A41.53 (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria table). Using A41.50 + B96.1 is therefore a mis-specification (higher-risk for miscoding) when organism-specific sepsis code exists and the provider documents the organism. 3) POA flags appear incorrect for several conditions: the clinical timeline shows septic shock, respiratory failure/ARDS, and infected necrosis present at or shortly after presentation (ED/H&P note documents multi-organ dysfunction, high lactate, intubation, and vasopressor use on admission). However the claim has POA=N for key codes (K85.82, A41.50, J80). The Hospital Problem List, ED note, and Admission H&P all document these conditions at presentation (supporting POA=Y); POA indicators on the claim should be corrected to match the chart (e.g., R65.21 POA=Y per problem list/admission). The R65.21 policy also notes POA must reflect whether shock was present on admission vs developed later (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Medical - Septic Shock Confirmed on Admission Pathway). 4) Respiratory failure / ventilation coding is supported: objective oxygenation data (ABG/SpO2/PF ratios in the notes), procedure note of intubation, and documented ventilation duration/extubation day support J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) and the ventilator-duration procedure code (policy presumption that invasive mechanical ventilation attributed to respiratory failure satisfies objective criteria is met) (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx; see Presumption rule regarding mechanical ventilation). Action to correct coding (complete corrected sets): - Revised principal diagnosis (position 1): K85.82 - Other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis (infected necrosis explicitly documented and organism identified). Remove the uninfected necrosis code K85.11 and the unspecified K85.90 (both contradicted or redundant given documented infected necrosis). - Replace sepsis code A41.50 + organism code B96.1 with the organism-specific sepsis code A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) and retain R65.21 (severe sepsis/septic shock) as an additional MCC-level code because septic shock (vasopressor + lactate) is documented. - Correct POA flags to reflect these conditions were present on admission (per Admission H&P, ED note, and Hospital Problem List). Specifically: K85.82 POA=Y; R65.21 POA=Y; A41.53 POA=Y; J80 POA=Y (ARDS documented at/near admission). - Keep the remaining supported comorbidities (diverticulitis with perforation/abscess, gallstone disease, AKI, AF, new-onset diabetes, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, GERD) as coded where supported by chart/problem list. - Procedures as billed (endotracheal intubation, feeding device placement, percutaneous drainage(s), VARD-related PCS entries, PICC insertion/monitoring device, and ventilator >96 hours) are supported by procedure notes, progress notes, and the discharge summary; leave procedure list unchanged but recommend coding validation to align exact PCS root operations/approach with operative/procedure notes (e.g., VARD vs. "excision" language). Key citations (audit trail): - History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946 - "Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology."; and Active Problem List entry "2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae." - Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086 - "infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16," and "Extubation was successful on ICU day 18 following resolution of ARDS." - History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946 - laboratory data: "lactate 4.6 mmol/L." and orders: "Hemodynamics: aggressive volume resuscitation with balanced crystalloid; norepinephrine to MAP >= 65; monitor for abdominal compartment syndrome." - Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p. 44-44 - "Indication for Procedure: Respiratory failure from pancreatitis and pain" (supports endotracheal intubation and attribution to respiratory failure). - Hospital Problem List, Hospital Problem List, p. 9-9 - "Septic shock | R65.21 | 05/29/2026 | Resolved | Off vasopressors day 10." - Policy guidance: Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx (R65.21 validation criteria: vasopressor + lactate and organism identification pathways) and Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx (J96.01 presumption rule when invasive mechanical ventilation attributed to respiratory failure). Conclusion: The clinical record supports infected, gallstone-related necrotizing pancreatitis with Klebsiella pneumoniae sepsis and septic shock, respiratory failure requiring prolonged ventilation, and AKI. However, the submitted claim miscoded the pancreatitis specificity and sepsis organism specificity and has incorrect POA indicators on multiple high-severity codes. Therefore this claim is a Finding. The complete corrected diagnosis and procedure sets are provided below for reconciliation and resubmission. Documents cited above are available in the chart and are enumerated explicitly in evidence_cited for line-by-line audit verification.
rationale_letter: Re: DRG audit determination - MR_14 (Admission 05/29/2026) To: Coding/Medical Records Department, We completed a clinical audit of the inpatient record for MR_14. The audit found that several high-severity diagnosis codes on the claim are miscoded or mis-specified relative to the treating-provider documentation and governing coding policy. Specifically, the chart documents infected necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with an identified organism (Klebsiella pneumoniae), septic shock requiring vasopressors and with elevated lactate, and respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation over 96 consecutive hours. These clinical facts require more specific diagnosis coding than was billed. Finding (summary): - The principal diagnosis and pancreatitis coding are incorrect as submitted. The medical record documents infected pancreatic necrosis (Klebsiella pneumoniae) related to gallstones. The claim lists K85.90 (unspecified) as principal and also K85.11 (biliary pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) plus K85.82 (infected necrosis). The combined/bundled use of an "uninfected necrosis" code alongside documentation of infected necrosis is inconsistent with the clinical record and ICD-10-CM coding principles. The chart supports K85.82 (acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis) as the principal diagnosis. - Sepsis coding: the organism is identified (Klebsiella pneumoniae) and treated; therefore the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code is A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae). The claim's use of A41.50 (gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) plus B96.1 (Klebsiella as cause) is a mis-specification per the sepsis code selection guidance when an organism-specific A41 code is available. - POA indicators on the submitted claim do not match the chart. Documentation indicates septic shock, respiratory failure/ARDS, and infected necrosis were present at or very near admission; these should be flagged POA=Y where appropriate. Basis (clinical + policy excerpts relied upon): - Infected necrosis and identified organism: History & Physical (Admitting) active problem list includes "Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae" and imaging documents 40-50% pancreatic necrosis; Discharge summary documents source control (CT-guided drainage and VARD) and meropenem therapy for Klebsiella (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 861-946; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086). - Septic shock physiology on admission: lactate >2 and vasopressor orders documented (norepinephrine to MAP >= 65) and Hospital Problem List lists R65.21 with onset 05/29/2026 (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 861-946; Hospital Problem List, p. 9-9). Policy for R65.21 requires documentation of septic shock (vasopressor + lactate criteria) and an organism pathway when organism identified (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx). - Respiratory failure and >96-hour ventilation: procedure note documents intubation for respiratory failure and Discharge Summary documents extubation on ICU day 18 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086; Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p. 44-44). The J96.01 policy permits presumption of the objective hypoxemia criterion when invasive mechanical ventilation is documented and attributed to respiratory failure (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx). Correction required (what we changed): - Principal diagnosis (position 1): change to K85.82 - Other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis. Remove K85.90 (unspecified) and K85.11 (biliary acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) as inconsistent with documentation of infected necrosis. - Replace A41.50 + B96.1 with A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) and retain R65.21 for severe sepsis with septic shock (MCC), as vasopressors and elevated lactate are documented. - Correct POA flags to reflect that infected necrosis, septic shock, respiratory failure/ARDS were present on admission (POA=Y) per Admission H&P/ED notes and Hospital Problem List. - Retain and validate procedure codes related to intubation, >96-hour ventilator support, percutaneous drainage, VARD, feeding device insertion, and vascular/PICC monitoring device placement - these are supported by procedure notes and the discharge summary; coder validation should ensure PCS root operations/approach match operative/procedure detail. Corrected diagnosis set (complete, position 1 = principal): 1. K85.82 2. K57.21 3. K80.2 4. R65.21 5. A41.53 6. J96.01 7. J80 8. N17.9 9. I48.91 10. E11.6 11. K86.8 12. I10 13. E78.5 14. K21.9 Corrected procedure set (complete): - 0BH17EZ - Insertion of endotracheal airway into trachea, via natural or artificial opening - 0DH64UZ - Insertion of feeding device into stomach, percutaneous endoscopic approach - 0FBG3ZZ - Excision of pancreas, percutaneous approach (VARD/excision coding should be validated against operative note) - 0F9G30Z - Drainage of pancreas with drainage device, percutaneous approach - 0W9G3ZZ - Drainage of peritoneal cavity, percutaneous approach - 02HV33Z - Insertion of infusion device into superior vena cava, percutaneous approach (PICC/infusion device) - 03HY32Z - Insertion of monitoring device into upper artery, percutaneous approach (arterial line) - 5A1D90Z - Assistance with respiratory ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours Disposition documented: transfer to Long-Term Acute Care Hospital (Transfer Instructions / Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1082-1086). If you disagree with these corrections, please provide specific physician attestation or CDI documentation supporting the retained alternative codes (e.g., explicit provider documentation that necrosis was uninfected, or that Klebsiella was NOT the etiology of sepsis), and we will reconsider. Otherwise, please implement the corrected code set and POA indicators on the claim. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team
